claim: Apple's Services revenue reached an all-time record in fiscal 2023.
passage: Services net sales reached an all-time record of $85.2 billion in fiscal 2023, driven by growth in advertising, cloud and payment services.
rationale: Direct verbatim support in passage.

claim: Apple iPhone revenue grew 25% year-over-year in Greater China.
passage: Net sales in Greater China decreased 2% during 2023, primarily reflecting lower net sales of iPhone and Mac.
rationale: Passage directly contradicts claim (revenue decreased 2%, not grew 25%).

claim: Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud segment includes Azure and Windows Server products.
passage: Intelligent Cloud consists of our public, private, and hybrid server products and cloud services including Microsoft Azure, Windows Server, SQL Server, and GitHub.
rationale: Explicitly named in segment definition.

claim: Microsoft completed the acquisition of Activision Blizzard in fiscal 2022.
passage: On January 18, 2022, Microsoft announced its agreement to acquire Activision Blizzard, Inc. The acquisition closed on October 13, 2023 (fiscal 2024).
rationale: Passage says the deal was announced in 2022 but closed in fiscal 2024.

claim: NVIDIA's Data Center revenue expansion was primarily driven by the Hopper GPU architecture.
passage: Data Center revenue grew significantly, led by our NVIDIA HGX platform based on the Hopper architecture for generative AI workloads.
rationale: Hopper architecture explicitly credited for Data Center expansion.

claim: NVIDIA halted all research and development for autonomous vehicle platforms.
passage: Automotive revenue was $1.1 billion, up 21%, reflecting growth in self-driving platforms and AI cockpit solutions.
rationale: Passage confirms automotive/self-driving grew 21%, contradicting the claim.

claim: Amazon transitioned from a single national fulfillment network to eight regionalized fulfillment hubs.
passage: During 2023, we re-architected our fulfillment network from a single national fulfillment network to eight distinct, regionalized model networks.
rationale: Directly matches network restructuring details.

claim: AWS experienced negative operating income margins in the latest fiscal year.
passage: AWS operating income was $24.6 billion compared to $22.8 billion in the prior year, generating an operating margin of 27.1%.
rationale: Operating margin was positive 27.1% ($24.6B profit).

claim: Tesla recorded $1.79 billion from sales of automotive regulatory credits in 2023.
passage: Automotive regulatory credits revenue was $1.79 billion in 2023 compared to $1.78 billion in 2022.
rationale: Exact figure confirmed.

claim: Tesla ceased vehicle production at Gigafactory Shanghai due to local environmental bans.
passage: Gigafactory Shanghai continues to serve as our primary export hub, running at high capacity throughout the reporting period.
rationale: Shanghai factory ran at high capacity; no cessation occurred.

claim: JPMorgan Chase maintained a CET1 capital ratio of 15.0% at year-end.
passage: The Firm's Basel III Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 15.0% under the Standardized Approach at December 31, 2023.
rationale: Exact capital ratio supported.

claim: JPMorgan reported zero credit loss allowances across consumer credit card loans.
passage: The allowance for credit losses for consumer loans was $10.8 billion, reflecting anticipated credit card charge-offs.
rationale: Passage states allowance was $10.8 billion, not zero.

claim: Meta's Reality Labs incurred an operating loss exceeding $16 billion in 2023.
passage: Reality Labs segment operating loss was $16.12 billion in 2023 compared to $13.72 billion in 2022.
rationale: Supported by the $16.12B reported loss.

claim: Meta generated more revenue from Reality Labs hardware than Family of Apps advertising.
passage: Family of Apps revenue accounted for approximately 98% of total revenue, primarily consisting of advertising.
rationale: Family of Apps ad revenue was 98% of total revenue.

claim: ExxonMobil upstream earnings declined year-over-year primarily due to lower natural gas and crude oil prices.
passage: Upstream earnings were $21.3 billion, down $15.2 billion from 2022, driven primarily by lower natural gas realisations and crude prices.
rationale: Explicitly stated as primary earnings driver.

claim: ExxonMobil eliminated all long-term debt from its balance sheet.
passage: Total debt at year-end was $41.5 billion, representing a debt-to-capital ratio of 16%.
rationale: ExxonMobil had $41.5 billion in debt.

claim: Pfizer's Paxlovid and Comirnaty sales declined sharply compared to 2022 peaks.
passage: Global revenues from Comirnaty and Paxlovid declined $46.8 billion or 78% operational, as expected following unprecedented pandemic demand.
rationale: Directly supports the sharp decline.

claim: Pfizer acquired Seagen Inc. for $43 billion to expand its oncology pipeline.
passage: On December 14, 2023, Pfizer completed its acquisition of Seagen Inc. for approximately $43 billion, adding industry-leading ADC cancer therapies.
rationale: Transaction details and strategic purpose verified.

claim: Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales were flat with 0% growth in the fiscal year.
passage: Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales grew 17% in the fiscal year, driven by strength in store-fulfilled pickup and delivery.
rationale: Passage says eCommerce grew 17%, directly contradicting 0% growth.

claim: Walmart operated over 10,500 stores and clubs across 19 countries at fiscal year-end.
passage: As of January 31, 2024, Walmart operated approximately 10,616 stores and clubs in 19 countries under 46 banners.
rationale: Over 10,500 stores in 19 countries matches approximately 10,616.
